PERFORMANCE AT A GLANCE

Performance & look-ahead

Look-ahead is the future reference window, not inference latency. Each point represents an evaluated controller configuration.

03

THE IDEA

Precision that holds through motion.

Loco-manipulation asks more of a humanoid than reproducing a motion. Its hands must reach the right place, its feet must preserve support, and that accuracy must survive changes in posture and movement.

Anchor follows sparse targets from human motion without online retargeting. Curated robot references guide whole-body coordination during training, while feedback corrects execution errors without changing the intended motion representation.

60msreference look-aheadFour reference frames at 50 Hz

THE BENCHMARK

Measure what manipulation needs.

Three complementary tracks examine precision, sustained tracking, and the ability to reach and hold a target as whole-body demands change.

A IN-HOUSE

Structured combinations of upper-body actions, lower-body support, and locomotion.

B PUBLIC

Broader motion sources and behaviors for evaluating generalization.

C REACHABILITY
3,210references

Prescribed wrist targets across five posture groups, with stable foot support.

05

Simulation evaluation

Tracking precision, task success and stable support across complementary experiments.

Data & evaluation notes＋

G / L denote reference-input modes, independently of the scoring frame. Motion success requires sustained tracking: wrist and ankle position errors ≤10 cm, orientation errors ≤1 rad, and other body-position errors ≤25 cm. Mean errors use frames before the first 25 cm body-position failure.

Reachability uses robot-space references and requires successful global tracking with no slips, unwanted steps, or touchdowns.

07

TELEOPERATION & AUTONOMY

A shared foundation for human and robot intent.

A common sparse-reference interface connects different operators, capture devices, and higher-level policies to whole-body control.

Demonstration collection results＋

VISION · LANGUAGE · ACTION

Everyday tasks, whole-body solutions.

Time progresses from left to right →

A vision-language-action policy predicts sparse body-part targets and hand commands. Anchor executes the whole-body references in a closed loop. The architecture also supports a motion-token interface through reconstructed near-term targets.

Autonomous task success by interface＋
08

METHOD

Intent stays separate from correction.

Human motion specifies the targets. Curated robot motion guides coordination. Explicit error feedback supports precise execution.
